# Simplex midpoint margins and actual finite endpoint cap credit

Historical claim of scope (pending review here): proved finite geometric and cap-accounting theorem. The matrix count strengthens the already archived result in `candidate 3ebb848426a73808` by retaining an explicit positive coordinate margin. The main new conclusion is an integrated lower bound for actual minimized endpoint-pair cap costs. It is not a statement about all cap orientations or a proof of OC.

Let \(d\ge1\), \(N=d+1\), \(j=\lceil N/2\rceil\), and \(b=1/N\). Define

\[
 \delta_N=
 \begin{cases}
  1/4,&N=2,\\[2mm]
  N^{-N/[2(\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1)]}-1/N,&N\ge3.
 \end{cases}                                               \tag{1}
\]

In every case \(\delta_N>0\).

## 1. A quantitative stochastic-matrix determinant bound

Let \(P\) be an \(N\times N\) nonnegative column-stochastic matrix with

\[
                       |\det P|\ge2^{-(N-1)}.
\]

Let its row maxima, in decreasing order, be
\(p_1\ge\cdots\ge p_N\). Then at least \(j\) rows satisfy

\[
                            p_i\ge b+\delta_N.              \tag{2}
\]

For \(N\ge3\), replace the first row by the sum of all rows, obtaining an all-ones row without changing the determinant. For every remaining row \(i\), subtract \(p_i/2\) times the ones row. Its entries now lie in \([-p_i/2,p_i/2]\), so its norm is at most \(\sqrt N p_i/2\). Hadamard gives

\[
 |\det P|\le\frac{N^{N/2}}{2^{N-1}}\prod_{i=2}^Np_i.
\]

Since \(j\ge2\), the first \(j-2\) factors are at most one and the remaining \(N-j+1\) factors are at most \(p_j\). Hence

\[
 p_j\ge N^{-N/[2(N-j+1)]}
       =N^{-N/[2(\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1)]}.
\]

The exponent has magnitude strictly less than one, proving both (2) and positivity in (1). No classification of maximal determinants is used.

For \(N=2\), write the columns as \((x_1,1-x_1)\), \((x_2,1-x_2)\). Their determinant has absolute value \(|x_1-x_2|\ge1/2\). The two row maxima sum to \(1+|x_1-x_2|\ge3/2\), so one is at least \(3/4=b+\delta_2\).

Two further bounds are useful for keeping actual row data. If \(r_i\) is row \(i\)'s sum, then

\[
 |\det P|^2\le\prod_i\|P_{i\cdot}\|_2^2
             \le\prod_i(p_i r_i)\le\prod_i p_i,             \tag{3}
\]

because \(\sum_i r_i=N\) implies \(\prod_i r_i\le1\). Consequently
\(\prod_i p_i\ge4^{-(N-1)}\), and more generally the \(k\)-th largest row maximum is at least
\(4^{-(N-1)/(N-k+1)}\). Formula (3) is supplementary; (2) supplies the explicit margin needed below.

In particular every conclusion below remains valid with the larger margin

\[
 \delta_N^*=
 \max\left\{N^{-N/(2R)},\ 4^{-(N-1)/R}\right\}-1/N,
 \qquad R=\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1,\quad N\ge3,                 \tag{3a}
\]

and \(\delta_2^*=1/4\). This follows by applying the two order-statistic bounds to the same \(j\)-th row maximum. The second term makes \(\liminf_{N\to\infty}\delta_N^*\ge1/16\); no large-dimensional decay to zero is forced for this selected half of the rows. The simpler \(\delta_N\) in (1) is retained in the statements for readability.

## 2. Every point of a compatible small fiber has many large midpoint coordinates

Let \(B,C\subset\mathbb R^d\) be simplices of the same volume \(V>0\). Let \(A\subset\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body of volume \(a>0\), and assume

\[
                            (A+C)/2\subset B.               \tag{4}
\]

Let \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_N\) be the barycentric coordinate functions of \(B\). For each coordinate put

\[
 h_i=\max_C\lambda_i,\qquad \ell_i=\min_C\lambda_i,
 \qquad W_i=h_i-\ell_i>0.
\]

Fix any \(p\in A\). The body

\[
                            L_p=(p+C)/2
\]

is an actual simplex contained in \(B\), with volume \(2^{-d}V\). Its barycentric vertex matrix is nonnegative and column stochastic. Its absolute determinant is precisely \(|L_p|/|B|=2^{-d}\), by the usual simplex-volume determinant formula. Its row maxima are

\[
                     \max_{L_p}\lambda_i
                         =\frac{\lambda_i(p)+h_i}{2}.
\]

Thus (2), applied separately at **every** \(p\in A\), yields at least \(j\) indices for which

\[
                       \lambda_i(p)+h_i\ge2(b+\delta_N).    \tag{5}
\]

The set of indices is allowed to depend on \(p\). No common high-coordinate set across \(A\) is asserted or needed. Also \(L_p\subset B\) gives

\[
                               W_i\le2                    \tag{6}
\]

for every coordinate. Neither \(A\subset B\) nor \(C\subset B\) is assumed.

## 3. A finite endpoint-pair inequality before summing directions

Allow middle-fiber thresholds \(b_i\in\mathbb R\), and set

\[
 E_i(\beta)=|A\cap\{\lambda_i\ge b_i+\beta\}|
            +|C\cap\{\lambda_i\ge b_i-\beta\}|,
 \qquad e_i=\inf_{\beta\in\mathbb R} E_i(\beta).             \tag{7}
\]

These are the actual endpoint contributions of the ambient cap
\(\lambda_i(x)+\beta z\ge b_i\) on bases \(z=-1,+1\). The continuous normal remains the \(i\)-th middle-simplex facet normal, while the integer tilt \(\beta\) is unrestricted.

By Brunn–Minkowski and (4), \(a\le V\). Write

\[
 r=(a/V)^{1/d}\le1,\qquad T_i=2b_i-h_i+W_i r.
\]

Then the following pointwise-in-direction lower bound is exact:

\[
                \boxed{\ e_i\ge
                    |A\cap\{\lambda_i\ge T_i\}|.\ }        \tag{8}
\]

To prove it, a cap of \(C\) at threshold \(h_i-W_i r\) has volume at least \(V r^d=a\). Indeed, choose a maximizer \(x_i\in C\). The homothetic copy
\(x_i+r(C-x_i)\) lies in that cap and has volume \(r^d V\).

For any fixed \(\beta\), if the \(C\)-cap in (7) has volume at least \(a\), then \(E_i(\beta)\ge a\), which dominates the right side of (8). Otherwise its threshold satisfies

\[
 b_i-\beta>h_i-W_i r,
 \qquad b_i+\beta<T_i.
\]

The \(A\)-cap therefore contains \(A\cap\{\lambda_i\ge T_i\}\). This proves (8) for every tilt and then for the infimum. All caps are closed. The strict inequalities in this second branch arise from a strict mass comparison, and do not discard any boundary mass.

The infimum can also be replaced by a minimum: for sufficiently negative or positive tilt, the two endpoint contributions are exactly \((a,0)\) or \((0,V)\); on the intervening compact interval the cap volumes are continuous, because \(A,C\) are full dimensional and the barycentric functional is nonconstant.

## 4. Integrated endpoint credit without small diameter

Put

\[
                       \sigma=\max_i(b_i-b)_+.
\]

If

\[
                   \boxed{\ (a/V)^{1/d}+\sigma<\delta_N,\ } \tag{9}
\]

then

\[
              \boxed{\ \sum_{i=1}^N e_i\ge j a
                       =\lceil(d+1)/2\rceil\,a.\ }         \tag{10}
\]

For each \(p\in A\), use its at least \(j\) indices from (5). For every such index, (6) and (9) imply

\[
 \lambda_i(p)
 \ge2b+2\delta_N-h_i
 >2b_i-h_i+W_i r=T_i.
\]

Thus the sets \(A\cap\{\lambda_i\ge T_i\}\) cover every point of \(A\) with multiplicity at least \(j\). Integrating this pointwise inequality and applying (8) gives (10). This is where changing high-coordinate sets are handled: one sums their actual indicators, rather than demanding a single set of directions work throughout \(A\).

For the original middle centroid thresholds \(b_i=b\), condition (9) is simply
\(a/V<\delta_N^d\). No small-diameter, fixed shape, or point-limit assumption on \(A\) is needed. The endpoint simplex \(C\) may have any shape or position consistent with (4).

For \(d\ge2\), \(j/N\ge1/2>\gamma_d\), so (10) in particular gives \(\sum_i e_i>N\gamma_d a\). This is only a numerical comparison for the specified facet-direction costs; it is not a proof that a proposed perturbed center controls every ambient halfspace.

## 5. A separate exact full-credit criterion in one direction

For comparison with point-limit arguments, let
\(m_{A,i}=\min_A\lambda_i\) and \(D_i=m_{A,i}+h_i-2b_i\). Directly splitting according to whether the \(A\)-cap is full gives

\[
 e_i\ge\min\left\{a,
 V\left[\operatorname{clip}\left(\frac{D_i}{W_i},0,1\right)\right]^d\right\}.
\]

Consequently, if \(D_i\ge W_i(a/V)^{1/d}\), then \(e_i=a\). The upper bound \(e_i\le a\) follows by choosing a sufficiently negative tilt, so that all of \(A\) and none of the volume of \(C\) are captured. This is useful when \(A\) actually shrinks to a point. The stronger integrated result (10) does not require that shrinkage.

## 6. Exact scope

The compatible triple can be realized as the three integer fibers of the actual ambient convex body
\(\operatorname{conv}((-1,A)\cup(0,B)\cup(1,C))\): the only possible added middle section from the two endpoints is \((A+C)/2\subset B\), so the three fibers are exactly the prescribed bodies. Thus the costs in (7) are genuine mixed-volume endpoint costs, not formal measures.

The conclusion concerns the \(d+1\) continuous directions of the middle simplex's facets, with independently optimized integer tilts. Other continuous directions, the choice of a single center, and the full mixed-depth minimization require additional arguments. There is no OC claim here.

In particular, normalized cap fractions of the midpoint simplex are a different quantity from the costs (7). For example \(L=(B+v_0)/2\) has all coordinates high, but its sum of normalized facet-cap volumes is \(1+d(1-2/N)^d\), which can be below \(\gamma_d N/2\). This does not conflict with (10), whose terms are actual minimized endpoint-pair costs normalized by the small endpoint mass.
